title: Testing the Gemini 4 series on my personal benchmark
subtitle: Four variants, two harnesses, six 7/7 passes.
description: A 7-slide visual breakdown of all 6 Gemini 4 runs (Hydrogen, Neon, Argon, Carbon across Antigravity CLI and OMP): generational leap over 3.8 Flash, 4-variant trade-offs, harness ablation, cold-boot Ctrl-C depth, and field notes.

slides.headlinePrimary: Testing the Gemini 4 series on my personal benchmark.
slides.headlineMuted: Four variants, two harnesses, six 7/7 passes.
slides.lead: Hydrogen, Neon, Argon, and Carbon all swept **7/7** — with a **2.6×** spread in speed and **2.1×** spread in cost.

slides.label: GENERATIONAL LEAP
slides.headlineMuted: Gemini 4 cut turns by up to 66% vs 3.8 Flash.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #1 HARNESS ABLATION
slides.headlineMuted: Switching to OMP sped up both Argon and Carbon.

steps.title: Carbon: -28% time, -17% cost
steps.desc: Dropped from `88m / $7.16` on Antigravity CLI to `63m / $5.91` on OMP with fewer cache evictions (`2` vs `5`).

steps.title: Argon: faster, more parallel
steps.desc: Cut duration `61m → 53m` (`-13%`) as batching hit **1.86 tools/turn** — though larger context (`294k`) bumped cost `$3.37 → $3.97`.

steps.title: Different HTTP architecture
steps.desc: On OMP, both audited OTP 28 internals and built zero-dep `:gen_tcp`/`:ssl` clients; on AGY, Hydrogen & Neon reached for `Mint`.

callout.title: Harness Shapes Architecture & Cost
callout.body: Even with identical weights and `#high` effort, harness tooling shifted wall-clock time by up to **25 minutes**.

slides.label: CASE STUDY #2 COLD-BOOT CTRL-C
slides.headlinePrimary: Only Carbon closed the cold-boot race.
slides.headlineMuted: Where the slowest variant earned its keep.

steps.title: The shared 200–350 ms gap
steps.desc: `Hydrogen`, `Neon`, and `Argon` all passed post-boot PTY `Ctrl-C` probes, but left a `~200–350 ms` BEAM startup window open.

steps.title: Carbon's AGY handshake fix
steps.desc: Caught the `20–220 ms` boot race during release verification and added a two-file `CB_INTR_FILE` + `CB_READY_FILE` handshake.

steps.title: Carbon's OMP upfront fix
steps.desc: Audited OTP 28 source during preparation and solved boot-window `Ctrl-C` cleanly via `SIGUSR2` before writing S1.

callout.title: Speed vs. Edge-Case Depth
callout.body: **Hydrogen** (`34m`) and **Neon** (`44m`) are the daily-driver sweet spot; **Carbon** (`$5.91–$7.16`) caught the hardest boot-window race.

items.head: High 'tool error' rates are mostly TDD
items.text: `11%–15%` error rates look noisy, yet file edits were **100% clean** on AGY — most errors were intentional red-phase test runs (`17–18` on Carbon).

items.head: Mid-run API stalls & retries
items.text: Carbon hit a **19m57s** stream stall on AGY, Argon hit a **3m15s** S3 timeout, and Hydrogen weathered **6 transient 503s**.

items.head: Cache evictions cost real money
items.text: Five mid-run prefix cache evictions added **$1.65** to Carbon's AGY bill (`94.68%` cache hit vs `97.57%` on Argon OMP).

items.head: 2027 rates double the bill
items.text: At 2027 standard API pricing (`2×` 2026 rates), these `$3.37–$7.16` runs become **$6.74–$14.32**.

items.head: Default to Hydrogen or Neon
items.text: **Hydrogen** (`34m`, `$3.42`) wins on speed; **Neon** (`44m`, `$3.69`, `49/49` tests) wins on test depth and stability (`0` stalls).

items.head: Argon is the parallel-batching king
items.text: **1.53–1.86 tools/turn** cut turns to `131` and delivered the lowest cost in the family (**`$3.37`**).

items.head: Save Carbon for gnarly edge cases
items.text: Paying `2×` more only pays off when you need deep upfront audits like closing a `20–220 ms` cold-boot signal race.
